Owner of Coimbatore pet boarding facility booked after Indie dog dies under care due to alleged negligence 

Updated - October 30, 2026 07:45 pm IST - COIMBATORE

The Hindu Bureau
SEE ALL Remove

The police have registered a case against the owner of a pet boarding centre at Saravanampatty in Coimbatore after an Indie dog lodged at the facility for care died of alleged negligence earlier this month.

Revathi Thangavel, owner of Cuddle Club House – Cage Free Dog Boarding and Grooming, was booked for offence under Section 11 (treating animals cruelly) of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, based on a complaint lodged by Adarsh Chandrasekaran, a resident of Fathima Nagar at Saravanampatty.

According to the police, the complainant had been rearing an Indie dog, namely Chikku, for the past two years. The dog was left at the boarding centre at 7 p.m. on September 30, 2026 after which the complainant travelled out of town. The centre informed him around 7.30 a.m. on October 4 over the phone that his pet dog had died.

The complainant visited the centre and examined surveillance cameras visuals. He found that his dog had attempted to jump over a gate around 6.45 p.m. on October 3, during which its collar got entangled in a rod, remained hanging, and died. The employees of the centre came to know about the incident only when they arrived the next morning, the police said.

The complainant lodged a complaint at the Saravanampatty police station, accusing the centre of having failed to provide round-the-clock surveillance and safe boarding facilities to dogs as they advertised. The police registered a case against the centre’s owner on Wednesday, October 28. Further investigation is on.
